3. Short facts of the plaintiff's case is that the predecessor of the opposite party No. 1 (ka)-1 (Thha) and opposite party No.2 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 181 of 1994 for declaration and for permanent injunction on 28-6-1994 before the Court of Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, against the petitioners and other opposite parties stating the 8044 acres including 5.68 acres land of CS Plot No. 158 of CS khatian No. 4 Mouza Razabazr under Original PS Keranigonj at present Tejgaon originality belonged to Abdul Quader. Said Abdul Quader sold out the entire property of the said CS Khatian No.4 to Babu Sarat Chandra Ghosh Ukil by a sale deed executed and-registered on 11-1-1921 and 12- 1-1921 respectively vide deed No. 351 and obtained possession. The said Babu Sarat Chandra Ghosh Ukil while owning and possessing the said land made a will on 24, Ashar 1335 BS to the benefit of Premtosh Ghosh and Bemola Charan Ghosh to the extent of eight anna share each. After the death of the said Sarat Chandra Ghosh Ukil, they filed Probate Case No. 7 of 1934 and obtained probate, said Premtosh Ghosh and Bemola Charan Ghosh being owners and possessors of the said property sold 35 decimals of land from the eastern portion of CS Plot No. 158 to Sk Jainuddin by Registered sale deed No. 4031 dated 18-10-1946. Thereafter Sheikh Jainuddin sold said 35 decimals of land to Abdul Khaleque by registered sale deed dated 14-2-1956 and delivered possession. SA Khatian No. 184 was prepared and published in the name of Abdul Khaleque the predecessor of present opposite party No.1 (ka) to 1 (Thha) in respect of 38 decimals of land. Though he has purchased 35 decimals of land and Premtosh Ghosh sold 9 pakhi 2 gonda land from CS Plot No. 158 and some others plot to Harendra Pal and Surjja Kanto Pal on 24-9-1946. Said Surjja Kanto Pal sold 2 pakhi land to Sheikh Hasenuddin on 14-11-1947. After the death of Sheikh Hasenuddin his heirs and Samiruddin sold 35 decimals of land to Ali Ahmed and Noor Mohammand on 10-5- 1054 and said Ali Ahmed and Noor Mohammad sold 18.5 decimals to Mirja Wasimuddin and 16.5 decimals to plaintiff Respondent No.1 Abdul Khaleque. Abdul Khaleque thereafter sold 16.5 decimals to said Mirja Wasimuddin on 2-6-1959. Mirja Wasimuddin sold 10 decimals to plaintiff respondent No.2 Amina Khaleque on 29-9-1978 and 24- 10-1978 by two sale deeds. In this way the plaintiffs became the owner in possession of 48 decimals of land. For construction of Pantha Path (West). Notice under LA Case No 40 -A/89-90 was issued upon the plaintiff No. 1 for acquisition of 4 decimals of land. Another notice was issued for acquisition of 42 decimals from CS Plot No. 158 upon plaintiff No.2. The plaintiff No. 1 constructed a tin-shed house measuring 80' long and some others semi-pacca house in the middle portion of his plot and let out the same to the monthly tenants. Plaintiff No. 1 gifted 12 and 1/2 decimals of land in favour of his daughter Jebunnessa and delivered possession and he remained owner and possessor or 25 and 3/4 decimals of land. All on a sudden RAJUK, Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and Land Acquisition Authority came to north western portion of CS Plot No. 158 with bulldozers and demolished his semi-pacca tin sheds and forcibly took possession of 20 decimals land out of 25 and 3/4 decimals of Plaintiff No. 1 and around 9 decimals of land out of 10 decimals of plaintiff No. 2 and materialized the same with Pantha Path (West). The action taken by LA authority and RAJUK are illegal, consequently plaintiff No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 184 of 1993 before the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, for declaration of his right for compensation and plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 being owners in possession of 6-3\4 decimals in suit plot adjacent to Pantha Path west in triangular shape. In the southern portion of CS Plot No. 155 the defendant Nos. 5 and 6 have their semi-pacca residential houses to the adjacent northern side of suit land. A portion of Panth Path (West) has gone through north western portion of CS Plot No. 158 and the defendants Nos. 1-4 (WASA authority) made an underground strong sewerage line just to the south of land alleged acquired portion of CS Plot No. 158 WASA had scheme to draw a connecting line from strong sewerage line to government khas canal through the small lane running through eastern middle portion of CS Plot No. 155. The plaintiffs came to learn in the last part of March 1994 that the place of said connecting line had been changed by defendant Nos. 1-4 at the instance of defendant Nos. 5 and 6 and that there is a boundary dispute between plaintiff No. 1 and defendant Nos.5 and 6 and a demarcating case No. 31 of 1994 which is pending. The acquired lands are the land of the plaintiffs who are the legal owner of the said land. The attempt of defendant Nos. 1-4 at the instance of defendant Nos. 5 and 6 to construct box and place sewerage line over the suit land is illegal, arbitrary and act of high handedness and prayed for permanent injunction against construction of sewerage line. But after the construction the said prayer was amended and new prayer for passing a decree for mandatory injunction directing the defendant Nos.1-4 to demolish and remove the sewerage line and box and defendant Nos. 5 and 6 to remove the semi-pacca room and the wall constructed in the suit land. 

 6. Further case of the defendant No.6 is that the suit land is khas land of the government and there was no communication or any link between the defendant No. 6 and defendant Nos. 1-4 in respect of the disputed land. The defendant No. 6 has purchased 5 and 29/60 decimals of land of SA Plot No. 46 of SA Khatian No. 79 corresponding to CS Plot No. 153 and 155 of CS Khatian No.6 of the suit Mouza in 1974 bounded on the South by khas khal land and defendant No.6 has been owning and possessing her said purchased land which is not within the suit land and the plaintiffs cannot get any relief against her and so the defendant No. 6 prayed for dismissal of the suit.
